workLog.action: Mirrored the canonical pytest.yml job contract
workLog.result: yaml.safe_load confirmed two jobs both named Run Python Tests: test (line 111) owning the Run pytest step (line 260) and skip-tests (line 427) owning the skip step (line 441). A name match alone cannot decide a verdict, so classification is by step name.

Stdlib-only resolver. Validates a 40-hex expected head, re-reads the live head from refs/pull/N/head, rejects stale heads and push runs, picks the latest run attempt, classifies executor versus pass-through jobs by step name, applies worst-wins severity across duplicate job names, and returns PASS, FAIL, SKIPPED, PENDING, STALE, CANCELLED, or UNKNOWN with a fixed-vocabulary reason. Argv-list subprocess calls, no shell.

workLog.action: Verified the resolver against live GitHub API payloads
workLog.result: Run 31360441685 reports run conclusion success with both Run Python Tests jobs success, yet the suite never ran; the resolver returns SKIPPED where a conclusion read would have returned PASS. Runs 31355229018, 31362376502, 31361938848, and 31360447277 resolve to PASS, CANCELLED, PENDING, and UNKNOWN respectively. End-to-end run against PR 4819 returned PASS with agreement AGREE.

57 tests covering stale head, push rejection, latest attempt, sibling failure wins, pass-through-only SKIPPED, pending, no run, cancelled, 403, malformed data, output sanitation, and the CLI contract. Includes a regression pin built from the real green-but-unrun payload.

One step appended to run-tests plus actions: read on that job. Existing outputs, step names, and check names are unchanged; the authoritative duplicate pytest run still executes. continue-on-error and an unconditional exit 0 keep the shadow step from changing any verdict.

nextSteps: Push the branch and open the PR; collect shadow agreement data across real pull requests.
Expect frequent PENDING versus PASS disagreements: pytest.yml has a 45 minute budget while ai-pr-quality-gate run-tests has 10 minutes. Measuring that rate is the point of phase 1.
Confirm actions: read suffices for the workflow GITHUB_TOKEN; local runs used a personal token.
Phase 2, only after the disagreement rate is understood: consume the resolved status and retire the duplicate run.
